extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal administration, USPTO stakeholders (patent/trademark practitioners), and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level performance, financial, and programmatic metrics and standards used in the USPTO FY2016 Performance and Accountability Report, including patent/trademark timeliness and quality measures, financial statement line items, and internal control/audit expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement line items and fiscal performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Key financial statement items reported (Fund Balance with Treasury; Property, Plant, and Equipment, Net; Other Assets; Total Assets; Deferred Revenue; Accounts Payable; Accrued Payroll, Benefits, and Leave; Other Liabilities; Total Liabilities; Net Position; Total Earned Revenue; Total Program Cost; Net Income from Operations; Budgetary Resources Available for Spending; Net Outlays; Federal Personnel; On-Time Payments to Vendors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the standard line items used to present the USPTO’s audited financial position and results. The report presents dollar amounts and percent changes year-over-year and ties these items to the audited financial statements. Financial reporting must produce complete, reliable, accurate, and consistent data and is subject to independent audit (the USPTO earned an unmodified audit opinion for FY2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Average First Action Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured in months; FY2016 Target shown (14.8) and FY2016 Actual (16.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate timeliness of initial patent examination actions. Targets are set annually; results are reported as met/slightly below/not met according to performance result thresholds. Reduction of first action pendency is a key element of Strategic Goal I to optimize patent timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Average Total Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured in months; FY2016 Target shown (25.4) and FY2016 Actual (25.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate total time from filing to disposition of patent applications. Targets feed into agency claims of backlog reduction and faster delivery of patent rights; reported under Strategic Goal I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average First Action Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured in months; FY2016 Target shown (2.5–3.5) and FY2016 Actual (3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate timeliness of initial trademark examining actions. Targets and actuals reported under Strategic Goal II to optimize trademark timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Average Total Pendency (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured in months; FY2016 Target shown (12.0) and FY2016 Actual (9.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors end-to-end trademark processing time. Shorter total pendency indicates more timely trademark registrations/decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark First Action Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of first actions on trademark applications meeting quality/compliance standards; FY2016 Target shown (95.5%) and FY2016 Actual (97.1%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quality metric for trademark examination. Higher compliance rates indicate greater adherence to substantive and procedural examination standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Final Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of final dispositions on trademark applications meeting quality/compliance standards; FY2016 Target shown (97.0%) and FY2016 Actual (97.8%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects accuracy and correctness of final trademark determinations and registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Office Action rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of patent office actions classified as 'Exceptional Office Action' (FY2016 Target 40.0% and FY2016 Actual 45.4%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a quality indicator for patent office actions; higher-than-target rates reported as 'Met' in FY2016. The metric tracks instances where an action is judged to be of exceptional quality according to agency review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Applications Processed Electronically
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of trademark applications processed through electronic systems; FY2016 Target 82.0% and FY2016 Actual 84.8%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures progress toward electronic filing/processing goals; used to incentivize electronic filing and reduce costs and processing time relative to paper filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country action-plan progress for prioritized countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which country teams have made progress on at least 75% of action steps in country-specific action plans along the following dimensions: institutional improvements of IP office administration; institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities; improvements in IP laws and regulations; establishment of government-to-government cooperative mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses USPTO international technical assistance outcomes. FY2016 Target 75% and FY2016 Actual 100%. Reporting is by country teams and covers multiple, enumerated dimensions of institutional and legal progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Foreign Government Officials Trained on Best Practices to Protect and Enforce IP
rubrics_metrics.description: A numerical target for training foreign officials (FY2016 Target 5,000; FY2016 Actual 4,975).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts participants in USPTO-led or sponsored international training programs; results mapped to 'Met/Slightly Below/Not Met' categories. Training outputs are used as indicators of global IP capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance result thresholds (met / slightly below / not met)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance result of a given measure is classified as: met (100% or greater of target), slightly below (95–99% of the target), or not met (below 95% of target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scoring rubric the USPTO uses to report whether a fiscal year performance target was achieved. Apply these thresholds to each quantitative measure to determine reported status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative (EPQI) — overall quality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPQI aims to improve patent quality by taking steps before, during, and after examination to ensure that patents issued are clear, consistent, and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality is judged across the prosecution lifecycle; initiatives include pilots and data-capture programs to identify best practices and training needs. The agency emphasizes both correctness of actions and clarity of reasoning in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record Pilot — record clarity criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot goal: identify and refine best practices for enhancing the clarity of the prosecution record with respect to claim interpretation, reasons for allowance, and interview summaries; encourages examiners to initiate pre-search interviews as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of prosecution documents (claim interpretation language, clear reasons for allowance/rejection, interview summaries) is a quality objective. Best practices identified by the pilot inform examiner training and are intended to improve the persuasiveness and durability of office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Correctness Data Capture program / Master Review Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Program to create an improved data capture system so reviewers consistently document results from reviews; Master Review Form standardizes reviews and places greater emphasis on assessing the clarity of an examiner’s reasoning while maintaining focus on correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized review forms and centralized data capture are used to measure and improve both clarity and correctness in examiner work products. Data drive targeted training and systemic improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Grant Outcomes Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot focusing on harnessing the art raised during PTAB AIA trials to enhance the examination of related applications and to identify best practices or deficiencies revealed by PTAB proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses post-grant trial outcomes to improve initial examination (e.g., identifying problematic areas or useful examination approaches) and to inform examiner training and practice changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents 4 Patients accelerated review eligibility and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast track review for cancer-treatment–related patents that aims to have final decisions made in 12 months or less; provides free, accelerated review open to any applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An initiative that sets an expedited timeliness standard (12 months for final decision) for a defined subject-matter class (cancer-treatment related). It is a procedural criterion for eligibility and prioritization of examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) work-sharing criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PPH, an applicant who receives a favorable ruling on patentability from one participating office may request that another participating office expedite examination of a commonly filed application to leverage work products and accelerate processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH participation is a mechanism-based criterion to accelerate examination across jurisdictions and improve multi-jurisdictional patent quality by relying on favorable findings from partner offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark fee alignment and electronic filing incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee proposal objectives: (1) better align fees with the full cost of products and services; (2) protect the integrity of the register by incentivizing more timely filing/examination and more efficient resolution of appeals and trials; (3) promote process efficiency through lower-cost electronic filing options than paper filing options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee-setting is used as a policy and performance lever to encourage behaviors (e.g., electronic filing, timeliness) that support agency strategic objectives; fee proposals are subjected to NPRM and stakeholder feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance data verification and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Information Section identifies key and supporting performance metrics and presents an overview of how performance data are verified and validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics reported must undergo verification and validation processes; the report describes those processes and commissioners’ performance. Verified/validated data underpin public reporting and OMB-required performance reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management assurances and internal controls / audit compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Management provides assurances on internal controls; independent auditors issue opinions, and the agency reports on material weaknesses or instances of non-compliance with laws and regulations (FY2016: unmodified opinion; auditors did not identify material weaknesses or instances of non-compliance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric for agency financial and control quality is compliance with audit standards (no material weaknesses), continuous improvement guided by OIG/GAO input, and statutory reporting obligations. Management must address 'Management Challenges' and maintain remediation plans where deficiencies exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog and examiner staffing metrics (backlog, examiner counts, attrition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational metrics include backlog of unexamined patent applications, reductions in backlog (e.g., from ~750,000 in 2009 to ~540,000 in FY2016), counts of patent examiners and trademark examining attorneys, and examiner attrition rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backlog and staffing metrics are used to evaluate capacity and timeliness. Examiner counts, attrition, and staffing-level tables support planning and are reported annually. Targets for backlog reduction and examiner hiring/retention are components of strategic planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework and IT operational resilience metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational capability metric: percent of workforce able to telework during disruptions (example: 77% of total USPTO workforce was able to telework at peak times during a blizzard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures IT readiness, continuity of operations, and telework program effectiveness. High telework capability is presented as a cost-saving and continuity success factor.
